author: M. O. Marshall
title: Five Troy men's tennis players named to All-Sun Belt teams - Wiregrass Times
text:
Five members of the Troy University men’s tennis team were recognized with All-Sun Belt honors, according to an announcement from the conference on April 22.
The recognition highlights the achievements of student-athletes who contributed significantly to their team’s success during the season. The awards reflect both individual performances and strong doubles partnerships that helped Troy reach new milestones.
Yeray Andres Pastor and Ausias Martin Melo were selected for the All-Sun Belt Singles Second Team. Pastor, Troy’s only senior this season, posted a 15-7 record in dual play, including a notable 12-2 mark on Court 3. He achieved an 11-match win streak from March 7 to April 14 and secured a key victory in the Sun Belt semifinals against Georgia Southern, helping Troy reach its first championship match since 2015. Head coach Rolando Vargas said, “Yeray was our leader and captain this season. In very important matches, he showed a lot of poise and experience. With that leadership, he was able to push his teammates around him. He finished his career playing for a title. The improvement and commitment that he showed certainly paid off.”
Martin Melo impressed in his debut season at Troy with a matching 15-7 record in dual play, mainly competing on Court 1 where he went 13-5. From March 19 to April 14, Martin Melo won nine consecutive matches—including wins over Mercer and Southern Miss—and also contributed with a semifinal win over Georgia Southern. Vargas said about Martin Melo: “Outstanding year for Ausias as a freshman to step up to Court 1. His improvement was outstanding, and he played with a lot of heart. The results definitely showed given his impressive record.”
In doubles competition, Luciano Alcocer paired with Pastor for First Team honors after qualifying for the ITA Sectional Championships following their run to the semifinals at ITA Southern Regional—despite only partnering three times during spring competition. Vargas commented: “It was a tremendous year for this duo after having a record-breaking result in regionals… Just an amazing year for them.” Thiago Drozdowski and Stephan Tavares Noale earned Doubles Second Team recognition by finishing spring play with a strong record of thirteen wins out of sixteen matches—including five victories in their last six contests—and played an important role by winning on Court 1 during the Sun Belt Championship match over Old Dominion.
Vargas said about Drozdowski and Tavares Noale: “This was a brand-new pair that started in the spring on Court 1… They’ve shown that they can play against anyone and helped us out a lot throughout the season… We couldn’t have done it without these two.”
